details: The overall cryptocurrency market has seen mixed performance, with the total market capitalization slightly decreasing. Bitcoin (BTC) is trading around $60,000, while Ethereum (ETH) is near $1,570. Market sentiment remains cautious, influenced by persistent outflows from U.S. spot Bitcoin and Ethereum ETFs. The Crypto Fear & Greed Index is currently at 15, indicating "Extreme Fear." Some altcoins, like Velvet and AGLDUSDT, have seen significant gains, while others, such as Worldcoin and PHBUSDT, have experienced sharp declines, highlighting high market volatility.
title: Crypto Market Experiences Mixed Performance Amid Continued Bearish Sentiment

details: Ethereum (ETH) is under considerable pressure, with its price down by 1.00% on June 28. On-chain data indicates "whale capitulation," as long-dormant wallets are moving ETH to sell, and major whale cohorts are reportedly in unrealized losses for the first time since 2019. This coincides with Tether (USDT) temporarily surpassing Ethereum's market cap on June 26, reflecting a rotation into stablecoins. U.S. spot Ethereum ETFs recorded their seventh consecutive day of net redemptions, with a weekly outflow of $273.34 million. Additionally, the "Glamsterdam" protocol upgrade has been delayed to late 2026, and the Ethereum Foundation announced workforce and budget reductions, raising concerns about future development.
title: Ethereum Faces Significant Pressure from Whale Capitulation and ETF Outflows

details: Binance is suspending some services for its European Union users as it will not secure a Markets in Crypto-Assets (MiCA) license by the July 1 deadline. This includes new registrations and certain restricted services. Rival exchanges, Coinbase and OKX, are actively offering sign-up bonuses and incentives to attract users transitioning from Binance. Coinbase, already MiCA-licensed since 2025, is offering a 5% transfer bonus for funds moved before July 13.
title: Binance Restricts EU Services as MiCA Deadline Looms; Competitors Offer Incentives

details: The average investor in BlackRock's spot Bitcoin ETF (IBIT) is now down approximately 40% as these funds experienced their second-worst week on record. This reflects the sustained negative demand for Bitcoin at the base layer, with apparent demand remaining negative for 208 consecutive days.
title: Average IBIT Investor Down 40% as Spot Bitcoin ETFs Record Second-Worst Week

details: Ripple has secured a preliminary Crypto-Asset Service Provider (CASP) license from Luxembourg's CSSF on June 23, 2026, under the EU MiCA framework, providing regulatory clarity for XRP in Europe. XRP spot ETFs have seen significant inflows, totaling $1.47 billion over seven consecutive weeks. The upcoming CLARITY Act deadline on July 18, 2026, could further codify XRP as a non-security, positively impacting its regulatory standing. Despite these positive developments, XRP's price remains 72% below its 2025 high.
title: XRP Gains Regulatory Clarity with MiCA License; ETF Inflows Continue

details: Coinbase Global's Base blockchain, a significant Ethereum Layer 2 network, suffered an outage of almost two hours. The disruption was caused by an invalid block that triggered a consensus failure, highlighting the technical risks associated with its single sequencer setup. Coinbase has since implemented a network upgrade to resolve the issue, and user funds were reported to be safe throughout the incident.
title: Coinbase's Base Blockchain Experiences Nearly Two-Hour Outage

details: Decrypt Media has announced the market debut of Securitize, a firm backed by BlackRock, marking a significant step in the tokenization landscape. This development is expected to reshape how securities are issued and traded, reflecting a growing institutional interest in tokenized assets and their potential impact on Wall Street and the broader financial ecosystem.
title: BlackRock-Backed Securitize Debuts, Signaling Growth in Tokenized Securities
